items.summary: ERC-8403提案将账户的全部授权（密钥、限额、时间锁）存为单一32字节Merkle根，增删或轮换密钥只需更新根，地址保持不变。该方案与签名算法无关，可接入后量子密钥，并配合EIP-8288的聚合STARK验证。
items.author: ethresearchbot
items.new_information: 单根管理授权，地址不变可接后量子密钥

evidence.quote: - ERC-8403 proposes a standard “authority lifecycle” for native account abstraction by representing all account authorities (keys or other predicates like limits/time locks) as Merkle-tree leaves and storing only a single 32-byte root in the account.

- Key add/rotate/revoke are unified into one action: update the root; the account address stays unchanged, but revocation speed depends on whether the account reads a recent named root (tier 1, cheaper but revokes lag) or reads current storage (tier 2, faster revoke but not in the cheap path).

- Post-quantum integration: ERC-8403 is signature-scheme-agnostic, so PQ keys can be leaves; combined with EIP-8288, PQ signatures can be validated via per-block aggregated STARKs, and an optional approach can move both “signature validity + membership under root” into a single proof at the cost of larger mempool payloads and upgrade/standardization

evidence.quote: 喜马拉雅资本创始人李录在哥伦比亚商学院第36届格雷厄姆与多德年度论坛上谈了不少AI。他认可这场技术革命的长期价值，但认为AI的发展可能经历不止一轮繁荣与崩溃。技术能走多远，除了取决于算力和算法，还受到资本投入、商业回报以及社会治理的约束。
这也解释了AI产业链不同环节的盈利差异。英伟达、博通、台积电等上游供应商，可以直接从芯片采购和制造订单中获得收入；微软、谷歌、Meta等大型科技公司则需要承担数据中心建设、设备折旧和运营成本，再通过云服务、广告效率提升和企业客户付费收回投资。模型厂商还要面对推理成本、价格竞争和持续研发投入。上游资本开支对应的订单增长，并不意味着下游能够同步获得相同规模的利润。
“上游资本开支对应的订单增长，并不意味着下游能够同步获得相同规模的利润”。反过来看，这恰恰是半导体的位置红利：AI产业链里，钱先流进芯片厂的口袋。再加上“新增信息分发的边际成本可以压得很低，但AI每生成一次回答、执行一次Agent任务，都需要继续消耗GPU算力、电力和存储资源”。算力需求不是一锤子买卖，是持续抽水。只要AI调用量还在涨，半导体的需求曲线就比市场想象的更长。
看半导体，别只看技术多性感，要看capex能不能持续、看下游客户的钱是不是真能赚回来。繁荣期吃肉，萧条期活下来。这才是这个行业的完整剧本。技术曲线向上，定价曲线震荡，中间每一轮崩溃都是对半导体持仓的极大考验。

evidence.quote: papertrade got exploited for $1.28M by 0x2025137a136bea7446deba681cbfc7cf1970840e within just 8 hours of being live.
how it works: papertrade prices every trade off hyperliquid's ETH price at that exact second. so if you can move hyperliquid's price for a few seconds, papertrade pays you for it.
the exploiter repeats this pattern over and over: long on papertrade, pump the price on hyperliquid, close the longs and open shorts on papertrade, dump the ETH back on hyperliquid, close the shorts.
296 wins out of 305 trades
same move as before. but this time the close never goes through. the short is stuck
02:31 ETH hits 2509.95. all 30 shorts liquidated, -$450k
leaving them with $1.28m of profit.

my guess is the team blocked 0x2025's closes to stop the attack. this is a temporary fix, the underlying oracle of papertrade is still identical, and vulnerable to the exact same manipulation which anyone could re-create from a fresh wallet.

evidence.quote: However, as aggressive loss farming gives way to delta-neutral farming, protocol revenue (traders’ net losses) falls, and so does the effective price of minting PAPER relative to a real loss.

That’s why, while minting PAPER should now cost about 2.7x what it did at launch, what stakers actually receive for each new PAPER has fallen, to about $2 per 1,000 new PAPER since the rush from nearly $5 during it.
Adjusted for inflation, each staked PAPER now earns about 98% less per hour than during the rush. The planned increase in the pool cap from $5M to $10M will cut staker payouts further.

This is not to say staked PAPER won’t keep earning decent yields, but the extremely fast paybacks are over, and with them the reason to rush in and farm PAPER through pure losses. Anything you do now should be purely delta neutral, ideally on lowish leverage so you can close on bigger moves and avoid the insane haircuts.

items.author: hkuppy
items.new_information: 以周期行业框架论证算力亏损将加速

evidence.quote: In a normal functioning ecosystem, when the price of tokens drops below the cost of production, the quantity of tokens declines to normalize with pricing. In this case, nothing in AI has any unit economics and you don’t see normalization because everyone is still going full-speed ahead with external funding. (Sort of like shale oil in 2016-2019). Meanwhile,
compute prices are based on LT contracts that were signed at above market prices, and are now capital destructive. They’ll eventually catch down to token prices in free-fall.

What we’re seeing here is spot price negatively diverging from term pricing. Usually, when this happens in a cyclical industry, it’s INCREDIBLY BEARISH. Especially when there are take-or-pay contracts that make it difficult to ration supply at prices below cost. What we’re witnessing is a world where losses will accelerate, just as more supply comes online….
